A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mesoporous organo- inorganic hybrid materials are a promising class of materials, which may find application in catalytic hydrogenation reactions.
mesoporous organo- inorganic hybrid materials are promising supports for the preparation of highly active and selective heterogeneous catalysts for various hydrogenation reactions.
metal and metal sulfides nanoparticles, immobilized on organic supports – MPFs and PAs, are very efficient catalysts in selective hydrogenations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mesoporous hybrid materials can serve as a versatile platform for immobilization of catalytically active centers, which can be easily tuned for a specific application.
the mesoporous hybrid materials, obtained from cheap organic precursors, can be used as catalyst supports for various metal nanoparticles, and can be used in various reactions of organic synthesis.
the use of organic supports in catalysis can be beneficial in the case of hydrogenation of aromatic and heteroaromatic substrates.
